changes.before: The first: claiming, revision and withdrawal are first-person constituting acts, and there is no set of external signatures both necessary and sufficient and portable to someone else. Two candidates were already ruled out. Verbal declaration is not necessary, because many value-contents are embodied and tacit. A durable preference is not sufficient, because a liking can hold thirty years and never be claimed. More generally, the third person cannot exhaustively verify whether an avowal occurred, so external evidence does not close into a final criterion. Facts about the relational structure really are readable: whether the candidate field is filled, whether a denial can be registered as a denial, whether the paths of revision and withdrawal are open. Reading those is not the same as being able to determine.

changes.before: The question a reader most wants to ask at this point is am I regressing. The question's presupposition does not hold. It presupposes that the centre of gravity moving toward rows earlier in the structural order could be a loss, and that cannot be a loss: structural order is not value order, and going back costs nothing. This is not a refusal to answer. It is that what the question asks about has no place in the structure.

disposition: Retain full existing English with seven localized scope/reference fixes. All 139 units and both tables compared. Preserves accumulation vs diachronic constitution, three reading domains, externally/self/no-one maintained closure, recovery vs first gaining, two cuts of fading, per-action centre of gravity, output/position independence, and no transition law or compulsory uptake.
limitations: Semantic source alignment, not proof of the theory.
